a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks cell voltage degradation and stack leak rate as indicators of anode failure. My observable is the anode microstructural strain rate inferred from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) phase angle shifts at the nickel oxidation/reduction peaks, which directly tracks the volume change kinetics that precede mechanical failure. This connects to failure physics because the rate of nickel oxidation during startup correlates with the magnitude of anode expansion and subsequent microstructural damage.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the relationship between EIS phase angle (θ) and strain rate (dε/dt): dε/dt = K × tan(θ), where K is a calibration constant derived from the known volume change of nickel during oxidation (ΔV/V = 0.42 for Ni→NiO). At 750°C, the calculated threshold is tan(θ) > 0.05 corresponding to strain rates > 2×10^-4 s^-1, which exceeds the anode's creep relaxation rate and will cause cumulative damage. This magnitude is consistent with reported nickel coarsening rates in SOFC anodes.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) Existing high-precision impedance analyzer (Solartron 1260), 2) Standard cell voltage measurement system, 3) Data acquisition system with 10 Hz sampling, 4) Custom analysis software (Python-based). Materials: None required beyond existing test setup. Instruments: All commercially available. Procedure: During each startup, apply 10 mV AC perturbation at 1 Hz-100 kHz frequency range while monitoring phase angle shift at the 50 Hz nickel oxidation peak (characteristic of Ni/NiO transition). Calculate tan(θ) and compare to threshold. No new hardware required.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: Same as standard practice (uses existing EIS capability). Operability: Requires additional 5 minutes per cycle for measurement (negligible impact). Maintenance: No additional maintenance burden (same equipment). Cost class: Same as standard practice (uses existing instrumentation). The only difference is the analysis software, which is off-the-shelf with custom scripting (minimal cost). Expected conclusion: Same deployment burden, different observable that detects failure precursors earlier than voltage degradation or leak rate.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Subject 5 cells to 200 start-stop cycles at 750°C with controlled heating/cooling rates (5°C/min). Instrumentation: EIS system with phase angle monitoring, voltage measurement, and acoustic emission detection for crack formation. Pass/fail threshold: Cell passes if after 200 cycles, power density ≥0.35 W/cm² at 0.7V and tan(θ) < 0.05 during all startups. Duration: 6 months (accelerated testing). Kill criterion: Any cell showing tan(θ) > 0.05 during 3 consecutive startups or power density <0.35 W/cm² before 200 cycles fails the test.
